title: The Lost Little Seahorse
summary: Marino is the slowest swimmer in the sea. One day he lets go of the reef to chase some bubbles, and the water carries him far, far from home.

scenes.text:
Marino was a little yellow seahorse with a small orange crest on his head.

Seahorses are the slowest swimmers in the whole ocean. That's why they spend the day holding on to the corals, with their tails curled tight, so the water won't carry them away.

"Never let go of the reef," his mum always told him.

And Marino never did.

Until that afternoon, when right in front of him floated a line of bubbles.

They were round and shiny, every colour there is, like glass marbles.

Marino stretched out his snout to touch one. And without even noticing, he let go.

He chased one bubble. And another. And another.

When the last one popped on his nose, Marino looked around.

There were no corals. There was no reef. Only blue water, above, below and on every side.

He tried to swim back. He fluttered the fin on his back as fast as he could… and hardly moved at all.

Then, all of a sudden, the water gave him a shove.

It was a current, strong and cold, and it dragged him even further away.

Marino found a strand of seaweed and wrapped his tail around it, very tight. And there he stayed, trembling, not knowing what to do.

After a while, a big shadow passed overhead. Marino shrank back.

But it wasn't a shark. It was a very old turtle, with lots of little lines on her shell.

"Well, look at that," she said. "A seahorse, so far from the corals? You must be lost."

"I let go," said Marino, in a tiny voice. "I live on the reef with the pink corals. But I'm very slow, and I'll never get there."

The turtle gave a slow little chuckle.

"I'm slow too. My name's Tula. And slow creatures have a trick. Do you want to see it?"

Tula swam to a place where the water was moving fast, like a river inside the sea.

"This one is warm," she said, "and it goes straight to the pink corals. Hold on."

Marino curled his tail around the edge of her shell.

And the current swept them away.

How fast they went! They passed stripy fish, an octopus who waved goodbye with all eight arms, and a dolphin who swam alongside them for a while, leaping out of the water.

Marino, the slowest swimmer in the ocean, was going faster than ever. And for the first time all afternoon, he burst out laughing.

At sunset, out of the blue, some pink corals appeared.

"It's my home!" shouted Marino.

His mum was at the edge of the reef, searching everywhere. When she saw him, she swam towards him as fast as a seahorse can swim, which isn't very fast at all. But to Marino it seemed like lightning.

They curled their tails together, which is how seahorses hug.

The clownfish next door popped out of his anemone to say hello. Tula waved a flipper goodbye and went on her way, slowly.

That night, Marino held on to his coral as always. But before he fell asleep, he spent a while watching the water flow by. Now he knew that water can be a road, too.
